convention.cycle_vs_toggle: a cycle is one rise + one fall; a toggle is one edge; a rise is the 0 -> 1 edge. A capacitor C takes C.VDD^2 from the rail on the rise and nothing on the fall, so a toggle -- the per-edge average -- costs 0.5 C VDD^2
convention.electrons: charge / e, with charge = energy / VDD and e = 1.602176634e-19 C
convention.electrons_of_a_board_figure: a board energy is not delivered at the die's rail, so its electron count is a convention, not a measurement. Every electron figure here divides by the same 0.517 V. The cards that produced E60, E65 and E38 ran at 521.9 mV, so an electron count taken at their own rail would be 0.9% lower.
convention.energy: the energy drawn from VDD by one event, at 0.517 V (the minion rail)
convention.note_on_E60s_electron_column: docs/reports/data/2026-10-20-bitflip-ladder/reduce.txt prints electrons as C.V/e, i.e. 2E/(V.e) -- the charge of the equivalent capacitor. Under the convention here (E/(V.e)) every one of its electron figures halves. Both appear below, labelled.
convention.temperature: 25 C for every SPICE number (ASAP7's TT corner); the die temperature only enters Landauer's floor, where it is stated
convention.which_unit_each_section_uses: one_transistor_switching and the_floor's rungs are PER RISE (C.VDD^2), because that is what a device deck measures. one_physical_net_toggle is PER TOGGLE (0.5 C VDD^2), because that is what the SAIF counts; its C_total_fF x VDD^2 gives the per-rise figure, exactly twice the per-toggle one. up_to_the_board's figures are sums over a whole event and belong to neither unit.

one_physical_net_toggle.the_wire_is_a_lower_bound: RETIRED Tue 27 Oct 2026 by Q129(a) -- it is NOT a lower bound, and this key's name is historical. The between-cell capacitance here is the global-route Steiner estimate, and that estimate is not coupling-free: the ORFS asap7 setRC.tcl hands it 0.1658 fF/um for a signal wire, a layer's TOTAL capacitance at nominal spacing with the neighbour coupling already bundled in and grounded. Detailed routing now closes and OpenRCX extraction puts the estimate 20-23% ABOVE the extraction at Miller k=1 (14,427 against 12,006 fF on the mixed netlist, +20.2%; 15,533 against 12,605 on this kept one, +23.2%), with coupling 58% of the k=1 wire capacitance each driver sees. So the wire share here is a CEILING and the transistor share a FLOOR: scaling this section's own split by that measured ratio moves the signal-net transistor share from 21.7% to about 23.4% and the clock-net one from 17.1% to about 20.2% -- a scaling, not a re-measurement. See docs/reports/data/2026-10-27-q129-routed-netlist/.
one_physical_net_toggle.what: what one toggle of one physical net in the TensorFMA32 lane charges, activity-weighted over a random fp32 multiply-add

charge_returns_at_the_fall.comment: the integrator comes back to zero, so the gate is a capacitor: nothing is lost in the device itself, the energy is lost in whatever drives it

in_a_real_cell_mix_weighted.comment: a fin inside a working cell costs the driver MORE than the same fin measured alone, because the cell's output swings against the input (Miller) and the internal nodes move with it. That excess is real energy and it is transistor, not wire -- but it is not capacitance sitting on the net, so the capacitance split above uses the static figure instead. The per-hold-state spread in by_cell_pin is the size of the Miller term: a cell whose output cannot move in either state (AO21x1 driven on A1, MAJx2) shows none.
in_a_real_cell_mix_weighted.the_split_inside_the_pin: the liberty's pin capacitance was characterised on ASAP7's parasitic-extracted netlist; the SPICE here is the LVS (schematic) one. The ratio is what the cell's own layout interconnect adds to its transistors -- wire, inside the cell.
in_a_real_cell_mix_weighted.what: the same gate, measured at the pin of the cells this multiply-add actually drives (15 types, 88.3% of the toggle-weighted driven pins)

short_circuit_bracketed.verdict: the minimum is real at both rails: 300 ps at 0.517 V and 50 ps at 0.700 V. Over the whole 1 ps - 2 ns range the spread is 7.5% of a cycle at 0.517 V against 59% at 0.700 V, so short circuit is the term that blows up at the higher rail and is worth a couple of percent at the minion's. This inverter's own output edge into this load is 23.4 ps (20-80%), where it sits 2.2% above its minimum.
short_circuit_bracketed.what: the same inverter and load swept 1 ps to 2 ns of input edge, on one measurement window shared by every deck, with each input state's static leakage measured and subtracted (one-switch4.json)

short_circuit_share.measured_as: excess rail energy over the cheapest input edge, INVx1 at the 2.105 fF a real net carries, edges 1-100 ps
short_circuit_share.verdict: over the 1-100 ps edges this first sweep covers, the spread is at most 2.5% of the net's 0.608 fJ per cycle -- but at 0.517 V the curve was still falling at its slowest edge, so that was the sampled spread and not a bound. The extended sweep below finds the minimum.

the_floor.the_one_sentence: moving a single electron across this chip's 0.517 V rail already costs 25.5 Landauer quanta at the die's 66 C, and the smallest switch in the design -- one minimum transistor's gate -- moves 108 of them, so the floor is 2755x below one transistor and 1.8e+09 x below one random fp32 multiply-add at the board.
the_floor.unit: every single-edge rung here is ONE RISE (C.VDD^2 from the rail); the rungs from a flipped bit upwards are whole composite events. Section one_physical_net_toggle's per-toggle figures are half the two net rungs.
the_floor.what: Landauer's kT ln2, at the die's own temperature, against every rung

E38.what: E38/E39's registered V3-ABL-A values, three cards; the chain's 0.27 / 2.13 / 5.78 pJ are the three-card means of them (docs/findings/05-claims.md)

E65_not_closed_here.note: E65 prices 32 individual B-side bit positions and the flow-M flip. The open flow was only run on the ladder's own h = 0,1,2,4,8 rungs, so there is no like-for-like bottom-up number for a named bit position yet; running mktiles.sh on E65's own operand files would give one.
E65_not_closed_here.what: E65, aifoundry3, 600 MHz, 521.9 mV, per designed flipped bit at the board

lb.what: E60, busy partner A = pi, per designed flipped bit, same card

lq.what: E60, quiet partner A = 1.0, per designed flipped bit, aifoundry3 at 600 MHz and 521.9 mV, 4 passes

switching_by_what_it_charges_pJ.note: the cells' own internal energy (0.431 pJ) sits on top of all three and is not split here

per_random_fp32_multiply_add.what: one random fp32 multiply-add in one lane, against what the card pays for one over idle
per_random_fp32_multiply_add.zeros_caution: the open flow prices the zeros pattern at 0.217 pJ, against E38's 0.27 pJ over idle, but these are not the same quantity: the open flow's zeros figure is the ungated root of this lane's clock tree, which on a card is already inside the idle the measurement subtracts. Do not read it as 80% closure.

up_to_the_board.what_the_missing_energy_is: the bottom-up figure is a floor TWICE over (corrected Tue 27 Oct 2026 by Q129(a); it said three times): half the design's capacitance is unpriced (CTS and repair_design made those nets after the netlist was simulated), and the ledger covers one lane's arithmetic while the board pays for the register file's read ports, the operand bus, the result path and leakage as well. The third reason once given here -- that the between-cell wire has no coupling term -- is WITHDRAWN: the global-route Steiner estimate carries coupling already and runs 20-23% above the extraction, so extracting the wire moves 0.137 pJ OUT of 'accounted' and widens the gap (1.9465 -> 1.8094 pJ bottom-up, closure against the board 33.7% -> 31.3%). Of the two reasons that remain, the unpriced half got slightly worse on a routed design, 43.6% of the farads priced against 50.5%. See docs/reports/data/2026-10-27-q129-routed-netlist/.
